summary.title: Intel® Xeon® 6+ processors | Cloud-native & 5G performance
summary.one_liner: Intel's product page for Xeon 6+ E-core server processors, listing four SKUs (288 down to 144 cores) and claimed efficiency, density and crypto gains versus Xeon 6 with E-cores, each footnoted to unpublished test references.
keywords: total cost of ownership server cpu
takeaways: Xeon 6+ is positioned for cloud-native and 5G core workloads, with a focus on agent density and efficiency.
The listed lineup has four models (6990E+, 6980E+, 6970E+, 6960E+) with 144 to 288 cores, 330 W to 450 W TDP, and FCLGA7529 sockets, all slated for Q2'26.
Headline claims include up to 79% lower TCO versus Xeon 6 with E-cores, up to 2.5x throughput, and an average 15.2x crypto gain, each tied to footnoted test IDs.
Intel Application Energy Telemetry (AET) is offered for per-application CPU energy and activity visibility.
The page gives no benchmark methodology or public results; the footnotes point to a separate processor claims site, so the numbers are unverified.
summary.summary: This is Intel's product page for the Xeon 6+ processor family, aimed at cloud-native and 5G core deployments. It lists marketing claims (up to 79% TCO reduction, up to 2.5x throughput, 15.2x average crypto speedup versus Xeon 6 with E-cores, and up to 30% over unnamed competition) and a table of four E-core SKUs with core counts, clock speeds, cache, TDP and socket type. Each claim is footnoted to test IDs on a separate Intel processor claims page, and the page itself gives no methodology or public results. Treat it as a spec sheet and vendor claim source rather than independent measurement.
